title: Kunsthistorisches Museum: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works change the scale of looking, from Bruegel's busy worlds to a queen's almost motionless hands.
introduction:
The Tower of Babel is too large for its workers; a royal child's dress seems almost to reverse the proportions of the body inside it. Elsewhere, a portrait head is assembled from marine creatures. Scale repeatedly alters what the viewer recognises first.

This selection puts that process beside paintings of crowds and concentrated individual encounters. Bruegel lets an entire social world unfold through small actions. Holbein gives a restrained sitter the same sustained attention. The difference is not between important and incidental detail, but between ways of organising it: a figure can carry a painting alone, or acquire meaning through the many other bodies around it.
visitNote: The selection comes from the museum’s painting collection. Loans, conservation and gallery changes can affect access, so check current information before planning a visit around a particular picture. The order follows visual comparisons rather than a route through the building.

books.title: A Treatise on Painting
books.author: Leonardo da Vinci; translated by John Francis Rigaud
books.note: Leonardo’s observations on bodies, perspective and light offer ways to examine the arrangements here. They are especially useful beside the portraits and invented architecture, without implying a direct connection to every painter.

works.title: The Tower of Babel
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Tower of Babel. Image credit: Dguendel; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kunsthistorisches_Museum_Wien,_Pieter_Bruegel_d.%C3%84.,_der_Turmbau_zu_Babel.JPG. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The enormous circular structure dwarfs the workers and visitors who make its scale intelligible. Different stages of construction remain exposed across the walls, complicating its apparent regularity. Bruegel gives the project both monumental ambition and innumerable practical tasks. Moving from the whole tower to its tiny activities changes the image from a single building into a vast accumulation of work.

works.title: The Hunters in the Snow
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Hunters in the Snow. Image credit: Dudva; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pieter_Bruegel_the_Elder,_Hunters_in_the_Snow_(Winter).jpg. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The hunters and dogs descend from dark, closely placed trees toward a valley busy with skating figures. Their return occupies only one part of winter's wider life. The steep viewpoint permits both bodily fatigue nearby and activity far below to remain visible. Bruegel gives distance its own incidents instead of letting it dissolve into background scenery.

works.title: The Peasant Wedding
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Peasant Wedding. Image credit: Yelkrokoyade; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Le_repas_de_noce_Pieter_Brueghel_l%27Ancien.jpg. CC BY-SA 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The bride stays comparatively quiet while servers move food through the crowded barn. Repeated bowls and working hands establish the meal's rhythm. Bruegel makes celebration depend visibly on practical coordination: bodies must carry, bend, receive and eat. The occasion is therefore held together by the labour of feeding people as much as by its ceremonial centre.

works.title: The Art of Painting
works.credit: Johannes Vermeer. The Art of Painting. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The painter's back withholds his face while the curtain gives access to his carefully arranged room. Model, tiled floor, chandelier and wall map occupy measured distances. Vermeer turns the activity of representation into a subject that must itself be represented. The viewer sees a painter looking, but not from the painter's own position.

works.title: The Crowning with Thorns
works.credit: Caravaggio. The Crowning with Thorns. Image credit: Caravaggio. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Rods press toward Christ's bowed head while an armoured figure watches nearby. The contrast between exposed skin and protective metal makes vulnerability unevenly distributed within the close group. Caravaggio leaves little spare distance around the act. The observer's protected body becomes part of its meaning even without sharing the labour of inflicting the violence.

works.title: The Return of the Herd
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Return of the Herd. Image credit: Pieter Brueghel the Elder; Own work , Yelkrokoyade , Taken in 13 July 2012, 09:56:21. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:La_rentr%C3%A9e_des_troupeaux_Pieter_Brueghel_l%27Ancien.jpg. CC BY-SA 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The cattle move together across the foreground while hills and water extend well beyond their immediate route. Warm animal bodies separate from the colder distance under a changing sky. Bruegel ties seasonal work to a shared direction of movement. The larger landscape gives that practical task its conditions without reducing it to an incidental decorative procession.

works.title: The Fight Between Carnival and Lent
works.catalogueTitle: The Fight Between Carnival and Lent
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Fight Between Carnival and Lent. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The opposed groups in front belong to a square already full of food, games and smaller encounters. Their contest does not exhaust the town's activity. Bruegel gives rival customs a common environment, allowing surrounding behaviour to complicate the opposition. The painting becomes richer when the eye moves away from its apparent central duel and follows the occupations continuing around it.

works.title: Self-Portrait in a Convex Mirror
works.credit: Parmigianino. Self-portrait in a Convex Mirror. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The foreground hand expands while the room bends around the circular edge. Parmigianino preserves the convex mirror's distortion instead of correcting it into an ordinary likeness. The face remains recognisable within a space whose proportions depend on an optical device. The portrait shows both a person and the particular conditions under which that person becomes visible.

works.title: The Three Philosophers
works.credit: Giorgione. The Three Philosophers. Image credit: Giorgione; Yair Haklai Taken in 28 March 2010. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Giorgione-The_Three_Philosophers-Kunsthistorisches_Museum.jpg. CC BY-SA 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Different clothes and positions distinguish the three men, but their relationship does not resolve into one obvious action. The seated figure turns toward the dark rock while a landscape opens beyond. Giorgione gives intervals between bodies and setting unusual importance. The uncertainty is worth retaining; a confident invented conversation would close possibilities the picture leaves available.

works.title: Children’s Games
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. Children's Games. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Running, balancing and grappling occupy successive patches of the town's ground. Each group has its own bodily arrangement, but repetition makes play into an extensive social world. Bruegel allows the scene to be read locally or across the whole surface. Rules become visible through what bodies do together, without a single narrator explaining every game.

works.title: Saint Sebastian
works.credit: Andrea Mantegna. Saint Sebastian. Image credit: Andrea Mantegna; anagoria. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:1459_Mantegna_Heiliger_Sebastian_Kunsthistorisches_Museum_Wienanagoria.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Arrows mark pale flesh beside hard classical stone. Mantegna makes the materials differ sharply while repeated verticals hold the bound figure upright. The surrounding ruins introduce another kind of bodily analogy: architecture, too, can be damaged while retaining its form. The landscape beyond offers distance, but the immediate encounter remains between vulnerable skin and carved surfaces.

works.title: Jacopo Strada
works.credit: Titian. Portrait of Jacopo Strada. Image credit: Dguendel; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kunsthistorisches_Museum_Wien,_Tizian,_Jacopo_Strada.JPG. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Strada leans into an encounter with a small sculpture at hand, surrounded by books and collected things. Titian makes handling part of the sitter's public identity. Knowledge and possession are presented through activity, not merely through accessories lined up behind a motionless body. The forward movement gives the crowded environment a human direction.

works.title: Adoration of the Trinity
works.credit: Albrecht Dürer. Adoration of the Trinity. Image credit: Dguendel; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kunsthistorisches_Museum_Wien,_Albrecht_D%C3%BCrer,_Allerheiligenbild.JPG. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Distinct levels make the large assembly navigable. Heavenly figures establish the upper focus, worshippers gather below, and a narrow landscape supplies a farther earthly register. Dürer gives collective devotion an overall structure without requiring every face to lose its individuality. Broad divisions provide the order within which closer attention can discover separate people.

works.title: Jane Seymour
works.credit: Hans Holbein the Younger. Jane Seymour. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: Jewellery, fabric and headdress give the queen's rank a precise material form. Her joined hands and restrained face supply comparatively little movement, so small changes acquire greater importance. Holbein makes the costume highly informative without letting it replace the sitter. The portrait holds exact surfaces and controlled human presence in a carefully maintained balance.

works.title: Hercules and Omphale
works.credit: Bartholomeus Spranger. Herakles and Omphale. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/bartholomaus-spranger/herakles-and-omphale-1585
works.description: Transferred attributes alter the expected relation between the seated Hercules and the twisting female figure. Spranger makes reversal visible through both objects and pose. The elaborate turns keep the overlapping bodies readable beneath heavy drapery, while their exchanged roles complicate the familiar heroic hierarchy. Myth becomes a means of rearranging who displays which signs of power.

works.title: Schönbrunn Palace from the Garden
works.catalogueTitle: Imperial summer palace of Schönbrunn, garden façade
works.credit: Bernardo Bellotto. Imperial summer palace of Schönbrunn, garden façade. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/bernardo-bellotto/imperial-summer-palace-of-sch%C3%B6nbrunn-garden-fa%C3%A7ade-1758
works.description: The long façade provides a stable horizontal beyond the formal garden. Small visitors distribute movement across the paths, measuring the building without challenging its dominance. Bellotto's architectural precision accommodates a social setting. The palace remains imposing, but the figures establish how its grounds can be occupied rather than leaving it as a completely uninhabited elevation.

works.title: Infanta Margarita Aged Five
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of the Infanta Margarita Aged Five
works.credit: Diego Velázquez. Portrait of the Infanta Margarita Aged Five. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/diego-velazquez/portrait-of-the-infanta-margarita-aged-five-1656
works.description: The dress occupies far more space than the child's exposed head and hands. Its broad geometry makes royal representation a bodily condition she must inhabit. Bright trim and a flower direct attention across the costume, while the small face retains its individual scale. Velázquez shows childhood within the visual apparatus of rank, rather than outside it.

works.title: The Peasant Dance
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Peasant Dance. Image credit: Dguendel; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kunsthistorisches_Museum_Wien,_Pieter_Bruegel_d.%C3%84.,_Bauerntanz.JPG. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Raised feet and swinging arms bring the festival close enough for effort to become visible. The foreground dancers have a weight different from Bruegel's tiny skaters in the winter valley. Their interrupted movements fill the street alongside the bagpiper. Moving nearer changes the account of collective leisure from an extensive pattern into the demands of individual bodies.

works.title: Water
works.credit: Giuseppe Arcimboldo. Water. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Fish and shells remain identifiable even after they form the profile of a head. Arcimboldo keeps the picture dependent on two incompatible scales of recognition. Concentrating on a creature breaks the face apart; stepping back restores it. The composition works through this repeated alternation, not through a final solution that makes either reading unnecessary.

works.title: Portrait of a Young Woman, Called Laura
works.credit: Portrait of a Young Woman (Laura). WikiArt; Giorgione. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Laurel, fur-lined clothing and pale cloth are described more securely than the sitter's identity can be established. Her turn and the held garment place those surfaces close to exposed skin. Giorgione gives material relations a concentrated presence without supplying a complete biographical account. The conventional name should preserve that uncertainty rather than disguising it as a confirmed identification.

closingSections.title: Move between the whole and one detail
paragraphs: Try this with Babel's workers, a wedding server or one marine creature in *Water*. Returning to the whole should change the detail's role, not make it disappear. The works belong to the museum's collection, but this sequence is not a guaranteed gallery route; confirm current display and access before planning a visit.
